observationsNotFindings: This is the most quotation-heavy artifact of its class I have reviewed and it is the better for it. Where the G08 catalog quoted member names and a reserved-numbers object, this one also carries each class's full exactByteIntent and passProperty verbatim. That makes the catalog self-contained for a later fixture-authoring cycle while leaving nothing to the author's discretion - nine string comparisons, all exact.

The quoted material does most of the boundary work itself, which is worth the coordinator noticing. Each exactByteIntent carries its own routing away from adjacent gates: crash-injection sends repair-media to DR-G06, DR-G08 and DR-G11; conflicting-project-locks refuses same-project concurrent-analyze, live-lease activation and two-cache-writer classes and declines to fork DR-103 lockSchema; process-death excludes G21 process-tree kill, G09 grant linearization and G12 doctor cases. Those exclusions are inherited rather than authored here, and they are the reason this catalog does not drift into neighbouring rows.

The mechanism reservation is unusually well anchored. Live G18 v2 journalHonesty cites file 04 directly - 'the concrete lock/journal/lease mechanism is open' - so the six reserved mechanisms the catalog lists in whatIsNotAuthored are a live architectural reservation rather than this artifact's caution. A later cycle that wants to author fixtures here still cannot choose a journal format without a separate act.

Both review pins are single-reviewer with no Codex counterpart. DR-107's design standing, like DR-112's and DR-122's, now rests on Claude-only acceptances at the harness, the leftover join and this catalog. Nothing overstates - each pin says 'Codex not reviewed' - but the aggregate is visible only from the coordinator's position.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. The artifact is quotation almost end to end and every quotation is exact. namedCorpusNotAuthored equals live G18 v2 element-wise, and all three classes reproduce their memberVerbatim, exactByteIntent and passProperty byte-for-byte against live namedCorpusClasses - nine string comparisons, all passing. The class ids are not minted here either: crash-injection, conflicting-project-locks and process-death are live G18 v2 ids reproduced in order, and the slashJoiner appears on the crash-injection class only, exactly as in the source. I tested the mechanism prohibitions by probing for concrete artifacts rather than reading the denials - no O_ flags, fcntl, flock, renameat, mkstemp, CBOR, protobuf, schema or field specs, no byte layouts, and no filesystem paths at all; the only .json strings are the four source paths. Live G18 v2 journalHonesty independently confirms the standing by citing file 04 that the concrete lock/journal/lease mechanism is open. All three classes carry fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED and journalInvented false, and both obligations the catalog declines to close are live and open in the lifecycle leftover join, whose OBL-G18-FX-AUTHORING carries the same three classes. Two notes rather than findings: the absent file 08 token matches the authored-catalog convention rather than the leftover-join one, so no stale token is carried against a row that actually reads PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW; and unlike the two catalogs before it, neither review pin here is mine, though both remain single-reviewer with no Codex. 19 attacks run, 19 refuted.
